title: Durable ask-user checkpoints become a standard harness primitive by H1 2027
body: Simon Willison's datasette-agent 0.2a0, released June 10, adds a capability most autonomous-loop harnesses still lack: a tool that declares a context parameter receives a ToolContext object and can call await context.ask_user(...) to suspend the run and ask the operator a yes/no, multiple-choice, or free-text question instead of guessing, and the suspended conversation persists to the database and survives a server restart, so the half-finished run resumes once the human answers; a paired save_query tool writes agent-generated SQL as a stored query only after explicit human approval. This matters because it is not a UI confirmation popup but a durable, restart-surviving suspend/resume checkpoint implemented at the individual-tool level, which is exactly the human-in-the-loop primitive that durable-execution agent frameworks have been converging toward from the orchestration side. As agents move from chat into long-running unattended work, the failure mode shifts from a wrong answer to a wrong irreversible action taken with no chance to intervene, and the durable answer is to let any tool pause the loop, ask a question, and hold its state across process death until a person responds - a control surface that does not exist if the only checkpoints are ephemeral in-memory prompts that vanish on restart. The forward thesis is that this ask-user-and-survive-restart checkpoint hardens from a single open-source implementation into an expected, named feature of the major agent harnesses and coding-agent runtimes. The concrete, falsifiable landing: by H1 2027 at least two major agent harnesses or coding-agent frameworks (the strongest candidates being a Claude Code / Codex CLI / Cursor / Cline-class coding agent, an orchestration framework such as LangGraph or a durable-execution runtime like Temporal or Restate, or a managed agent platform like AWS Bedrock AgentCore or Microsoft Foundry) ship a documented mid-execution human-input primitive in which a running tool can suspend the agent, request a typed answer or approval from the operator, and resume the same run after a full process or server restart - state persisted, not re-prompted from scratch. A transient in-memory approval prompt, a pre-run permission allowlist, or an after-the-fact audit log does not count; the marker is a documented suspend-ask-resume checkpoint that durably survives restart, shipped by a non-Datasette stack.

reasoning.because: datasette-agent ToolContext.ask_user pauses a run to ask the operator; paused state survives restart
reasoning.given: long-running agents need durable human-in-the-loop checkpoints, not prompts that vanish on restart
reasoning.so_that: two-plus major harnesses ship a documented suspend-ask-resume human-input primitive that survives restart
reasoning.landing: by H1 2027; two-plus non-Datasette harnesses ship a restart-durable checkpoint
reasoning.plain_language: An open-source AI agent can pause, ask the human, and resume after a restart; big agent tools will copy it.

summary: datasette-agent 0.2 lets any tool suspend an agent run to ask the operator a question, with the paused conversation persisted so it survives a server restart and resumes once answered. Expect this durable checkpoint to become a standard primitive in two-plus major agent harnesses by H1 2027.
